documents: Attention mechanisms in neural networks have shown remarkable success in sequence-to-sequence tasks. We introduce the Transformer, a model architecture eschewing recurrence and instead relying entirely on an attention mechanism to draw global dependencies between input and output. The Transformer allows for significantly more parallelization and can reach a new state of the art in translation quality.

We present GPT-3, an autoregressive language model with 175 billion parameters, 10x more than any previous non-sparse language model. We test its performance in the few-shot setting, without any gradient updates or fine-tuning, with tasks and few-shot demonstrations specified purely via text interaction with the model.

Transfer learning has emerged as a powerful technique in natural language processing. We introduce BERT: Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers. BERT is designed to pre-train deep bidirectional representations from unlabeled text by jointly conditioning on both left and right context in all layers.

Deep residual learning has shown superior performance in image recognition tasks. We present residual learning frameworks to ease the training of networks that are substantially deeper than those used previously. We explicitly reformulate the layers as learning residual functions with reference to the layer inputs, instead of learning unreferenced functions.

Generative adversarial networks are a class of AI algorithms used in unsupervised machine learning, implemented by a system of two neural networks contesting with each other in a zero-sum game framework. This technique can generate photographs that look authentic to human observers, having many realistic characteristics.

We propose Adam, an algorithm for first-order gradient-based optimization of stochastic objective functions, based on adaptive estimates of lower-order moments. The method is straightforward to implement, is computationally efficient, has little memory requirements, is invariant to diagonal rescaling of the gradients, and is well suited for problems that are large in terms of data and parameters.

Convolutional networks have brought about breakthroughs in processing images, video, speech and audio, whereas recurrent networks have shone light on sequential data such as text and speech. We show that convolutional neural networks can be effectively used for sequence modeling tasks, achieving state-of-the-art accuracy while providing computational benefits.

Self-supervised learning enables AI systems to learn from vast quantities of data. We present a simple framework for contrastive learning of visual representations, which we call SimCLR. Our framework substantially outperforms previous work and matches or exceeds the performance of supervised learning on ImageNet.

We introduce a new language representation model called ELECTRA, which pre-trains text encoders as discriminators rather than generators. ELECTRA is more sample-efficient than masked language modeling because the model learns from all input tokens rather than just the small subset that was masked.

Vision transformers (ViT) demonstrate that a pure transformer applied directly to sequences of image patches can perform very well on image classification tasks. When pre-trained on large amounts of data and transferred to multiple recognition benchmarks, Vision Transformer attains excellent results compared to state-of-the-art convolutional networks.

We present masked autoencoders (MAE) as a scalable self-supervised learner for computer vision. Our approach is simple: we mask random patches of the input image and reconstruct the missing pixels. Coupling these two designs enables us to train large models efficiently and effectively.

Diffusion models have emerged as a powerful new family of deep generative models with record-breaking results in image synthesis and beyond. In this work, we show that diffusion models can be seen from the perspective of variational inference, providing a principled framework for model design and optimization.

We introduce CLIP (Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training), a neural network trained on a variety of (image, text) pairs. CLIP efficiently learns visual concepts from natural language supervision and can be applied to any visual classification benchmark by simply providing the names of the visual categories to be recognized.

Large language models have shown impressive capabilities in few-shot learning. We investigate the scaling laws for language model performance, studying how loss scales as a function of model size, dataset size, and the amount of compute used for training. We find that performance depends strongly on scale.

Reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) has proven effective for aligning language models with human preferences. We fine-tune language models to act as reward models and then use these to optimize a policy via reinforcement learning, resulting in models that are more helpful, honest, and harmless.

We present a method for meta-learning that is model-agnostic, in the sense that it is compatible with any model trained with gradient descent and applicable to a variety of different learning problems. Our algorithm trains a model's initial parameters such that the model has maximal performance after k gradient updates.

Neural architecture search (NAS) has shown impressive results in automating neural network design. We propose an efficient neural architecture search via parameter sharing, which speeds up NAS by orders of magnitude while maintaining competitive performance. Our method shares parameters among child models in the search space.

We introduce federated learning, a machine learning approach where a shared global model is trained across multiple decentralized devices holding local data samples, without exchanging them. This approach enables mobile phones to collaboratively learn a shared prediction model while keeping all the training data on the device.

Knowledge distillation is a process of transferring knowledge from a large model to a smaller one. We present DistilBERT, a distilled version of BERT that reduces the size by 40% while retaining 97% of its language understanding capabilities and being 60% faster.

We present Graph Neural Networks, which generate embeddings for nodes in a graph by aggregating features from neighboring nodes. GNNs are capable of learning representations of graphs and have shown strong performance on tasks including node classification, link prediction, and graph classification.

Explainability in deep learning remains a fundamental challenge. We introduce attention-based explanations and gradient-based visualization techniques that provide insight into which parts of the input most influence the model's predictions, improving model interpretability and trustworthiness.

We present neural ordinary differential equations (Neural ODEs), a new family of deep neural network models. Instead of specifying a discrete sequence of hidden layers, we parameterize the derivative of the hidden state using a neural network. This approach has memory cost advantages and can naturally incorporate time-continuous dynamics.

Zero-shot learning aims to recognize objects whose instances may not have been seen during training. We present a framework that learns to synthesize CNN features from semantic attributes, enabling classification of unseen classes. Our approach demonstrates the ability to scale to large numbers of unseen classes.

We introduce contrastive learning methods for self-supervised representation learning. By learning to maximize agreement between differently augmented views of the same data example, models can learn useful representations without requiring labels, achieving performance competitive with supervised methods.

Meta-learning, or learning to learn, is concerned with learning algorithms that can quickly adapt to new tasks. We present a probabilistic framework for meta-learning that is based on amortized variational inference, allowing for efficient adaptation with limited data from new tasks.

We present neural architecture transformers that automatically discover data augmentation policies. AutoAugment uses a search algorithm to find an optimal augmentation strategy for a target dataset, significantly improving generalization performance across image classification benchmarks.

Multimodal learning seeks to build models that can process and relate information from multiple modalities. We introduce approaches for learning joint embeddings of images and text, enabling applications such as image-text retrieval, visual question answering, and cross-modal generation.

We introduce prompt-based learning for large language models, where task descriptions are provided in natural language. This approach enables few-shot and zero-shot learning by properly designing prompts that elicit desired behaviors from pre-trained language models without fine-tuning.

Continual learning addresses the problem of learning new tasks sequentially without forgetting previous knowledge. We present elastic weight consolidation, which slows down learning on certain weights based on their importance to previously learned tasks, mitigating catastrophic forgetting.

We present neural machine translation models based on the Transformer architecture that achieve state-of-the-art results on multiple language pairs. Our models are more parallelizable and require significantly less time to train than recurrent architectures.

Active learning strategies aim to achieve high accuracy with minimal labeled data by strategically selecting the most informative examples for labeling. We present deep active learning methods that use neural network uncertainty estimates to guide the selection process.

We introduce normalizing flows, a class of generative models that learn invertible transformations between data and a simple base distribution. This approach enables exact likelihood computation and efficient sampling, with applications in density estimation and variational inference.

Text summarization aims to condense documents while preserving key information. We present neural abstractive summarization models based on sequence-to-sequence architectures with attention mechanisms, achieving human-level performance on benchmark datasets.

We present methods for adversarial training that improve model robustness. By training on adversarially perturbed examples, models learn to be invariant to small input perturbations, improving both adversarial robustness and generalization to natural distribution shifts.

Few-shot learning aims to learn from a limited number of examples. We introduce prototypical networks that learn a metric space in which classification can be performed by computing distances to prototype representations of each class, enabling effective few-shot classification.

We present neural processes, a class of models that can learn a distribution over functions. Neural processes combine the benefits of neural networks and Gaussian processes, providing a practical approach to uncertainty estimation and meta-learning.

Object detection aims to localize and classify objects in images. We introduce YOLO (You Only Look Once), a unified neural network that predicts bounding boxes and class probabilities directly from full images in one evaluation, achieving real-time detection speeds.

We present semantic segmentation methods based on fully convolutional networks that make predictions at every pixel. By combining deep learning with multi-scale processing and structured prediction, these models achieve state-of-the-art performance on benchmark datasets.

Neural architecture search can discover architectures that outperform hand-designed networks. We present efficient NAS methods that use evolutionary algorithms and reinforcement learning to search the architecture space, finding novel designs for image classification and beyond.

We introduce self-attention mechanisms that allow models to weigh the importance of different parts of the input when making predictions. Self-attention has become a fundamental building block in modern neural architectures, particularly for sequence modeling tasks.

Curriculum learning organizes training data from easy to difficult examples. We show that this approach can speed up convergence and improve final model performance by providing a structured learning trajectory that mimics human learning.

We present variational autoencoders (VAEs), a framework for learning latent variable models. VAEs combine variational inference with deep learning, enabling efficient learning of complex distributions and generation of high-quality samples.

Domain adaptation aims to transfer knowledge from a source domain to a different but related target domain. We introduce adversarial domain adaptation methods that align feature distributions across domains, improving model performance when training and test distributions differ.

We present neural style transfer methods that separate and recombine content and style of images. By optimizing images to match content from one source and style from another, these methods enable artistic image generation and manipulation.

Question answering systems aim to automatically answer questions posed in natural language. We introduce neural QA models that can read passages and extract or generate answers, achieving human-level performance on reading comprehension benchmarks.

We present pre-training methods for natural language processing that learn general-purpose representations from large text corpora. These pre-trained models can be fine-tuned for specific tasks with minimal task-specific architecture modifications.

Attention mechanisms for computer vision enable models to focus on relevant image regions. We introduce spatial transformer networks that learn to perform geometric transformations, improving model invariance to transformations and achieving better localization.

We present methods for neural language generation that produce fluent and coherent text. By combining large-scale pre-training with controlled generation techniques, these models can generate high-quality text for various applications.

Imbalanced classification deals with datasets where some classes are underrepresented. We introduce techniques including resampling, cost-sensitive learning, and focal loss that improve model performance on minority classes.

We present multi-task learning frameworks where models are trained to perform multiple related tasks simultaneously. By sharing representations across tasks, multi-task learning can improve generalization and sample efficiency.

Neural ordinary differential equations provide a continuous-depth framework for deep learning. By parameterizing hidden state derivatives, these models offer memory-efficient training and the ability to adapt model complexity to data complexity.

We introduce batch normalization, a technique to normalize layer inputs during training. This approach accelerates training, allows higher learning rates, and acts as a regularizer, improving model performance across various architectures.

Dropout is a regularization technique that randomly drops units during training to prevent overfitting. We show that dropout can be interpreted as approximate Bayesian inference, providing a principled approach to uncertainty estimation.

We present deep Q-networks (DQN), combining deep learning with reinforcement learning to learn control policies directly from high-dimensional sensory inputs. DQN achieves human-level performance on Atari games without game-specific feature engineering.

Policy gradient methods provide a framework for learning control policies through direct policy optimization. We introduce the REINFORCE algorithm and variance reduction techniques that enable stable policy learning in high-dimensional action spaces.

We present actor-critic methods that combine value-based and policy-based reinforcement learning. By maintaining both a policy and a value function, these methods achieve stable learning and strong performance on continuous control tasks.

Neural Turing Machines extend neural networks with external memory that can be read from and written to, enabling networks to learn algorithmic patterns and perform complex reasoning tasks that require explicit memory access.

We introduce capsule networks, a new type of neural network architecture that uses groups of neurons (capsules) to represent different properties of entities. Capsules preserve hierarchical spatial relationships and improve generalization.

Siamese networks learn to compare inputs by training on pairs of examples. We present applications of Siamese architectures to one-shot learning, signature verification, and metric learning, where learning a good similarity metric is crucial.

We present neural sequence models based on temporal convolutional networks that can capture long-range dependencies. These models offer an alternative to recurrent architectures with benefits including parallelizability and stable gradients.

Attention is all you need: we show that the Transformer architecture, based solely on attention mechanisms and feed-forward layers, can achieve state-of-the-art results in machine translation without recurrence or convolution.

We introduce LSTM (Long Short-Term Memory) networks, a recurrent neural network architecture designed to avoid the vanishing gradient problem. LSTMs can learn long-term dependencies and have become the standard for sequence modeling tasks.

We present GRU (Gated Recurrent Units), a simplified variant of LSTM that uses fewer parameters while maintaining similar performance. GRUs have become popular for sequence modeling due to their efficiency and effectiveness.

EfficientNet scales neural networks using a compound scaling method that uniformly scales depth, width, and resolution. This approach achieves better efficiency and accuracy trade-offs than conventional scaling methods.

We introduce MobileNets, efficient neural network architectures designed for mobile and embedded vision applications. Using depthwise separable convolutions, MobileNets reduce computation and model size while maintaining accuracy.

ResNeXt introduces a simple, highly modularized network architecture that aggregates a set of transformations with the same topology. This design pattern yields improved accuracy over ResNet with similar complexity.

We present DenseNet, where each layer is connected to every other layer in a feed-forward fashion. This architecture alleviates the vanishing gradient problem, strengthens feature propagation, and encourages feature reuse.

We introduce SqueezeNet, a small neural network architecture that achieves AlexNet-level accuracy with 50x fewer parameters. This work demonstrates that model size can be drastically reduced without sacrificing accuracy.

Neural architecture search using evolutionary algorithms can automatically discover high-performing architectures. We present methods that evolve architectures over generations, finding novel designs that outperform human-designed networks.

We present transfer learning approaches that leverage pre-trained models for new tasks. By initializing with weights learned on large datasets, transfer learning accelerates training and improves performance, especially with limited target data.

Data augmentation techniques artificially expand training datasets by applying transformations to existing examples. We present systematic approaches to data augmentation that improve model robustness and generalization.

We introduce mixup, a simple data augmentation technique that trains neural networks on convex combinations of pairs of examples and their labels. Mixup improves generalization and makes networks more robust to adversarial examples.

Label smoothing is a regularization technique that prevents neural networks from becoming overconfident. By using soft targets instead of hard labels, label smoothing improves model calibration and generalization.

We present learning rate schedules that adapt the learning rate during training. Techniques including learning rate warmup, cosine annealing, and step decay improve convergence and final model performance.

We introduce early stopping as a regularization technique that monitors validation performance and halts training when performance stops improving. This prevents overfitting and reduces unnecessary computation.

Ensemble methods combine multiple models to improve predictions. We present approaches including bagging, boosting, and stacking that leverage diverse models to achieve better accuracy and robustness than individual models.

We present gradient clipping techniques that prevent exploding gradients in neural network training. By limiting gradient magnitudes, these methods stabilize training of deep networks, particularly recurrent architectures.

Weight decay is a regularization technique that adds a penalty for large weights to the loss function. We show that weight decay in adaptive optimizers like Adam differs from L2 regularization, leading to improved methods like AdamW.

We introduce neural architecture optimization methods that treat architecture search as a continuous optimization problem. By relaxing the discrete search space, these methods enable efficient gradient-based architecture search.

Neural machine reading aims to teach machines to comprehend text and answer questions about it. We present models based on attention mechanisms that achieve strong performance on reading comprehension benchmarks.

We present named entity recognition models that identify and classify named entities in text. Using bidirectional LSTMs with conditional random fields, these models achieve state-of-the-art performance on benchmark datasets.

Relation extraction aims to identify semantic relationships between entities in text. We introduce neural models that use attention and dependency parsing to capture complex relationships, improving information extraction performance.

We present neural coreference resolution models that determine which mentions in text refer to the same entities. Using span representations and attention mechanisms, these models achieve human-level performance.

Sentiment analysis aims to determine the emotional tone of text. We introduce neural models that capture complex linguistic patterns and context, achieving state-of-the-art results on sentiment classification benchmarks.

We present neural dependency parsing models that predict syntactic structure of sentences. Using graph-based and transition-based approaches with neural networks, these models achieve highly accurate parsing.

Text classification assigns predefined categories to documents. We introduce neural models based on CNNs and RNNs that automatically learn relevant features, outperforming traditional feature engineering approaches.

We present neural language models that estimate the probability distribution of word sequences. By training on large corpora, these models learn rich representations of language that transfer to downstream tasks.

Word embeddings represent words as dense vectors that capture semantic relationships. We introduce Word2Vec and GloVe, methods for learning word embeddings from large text corpora using neural networks and co-occurrence statistics.

We present contextual word embeddings that generate different representations for words based on their context. ELMo uses bidirectional LSTMs to create context-dependent embeddings, improving performance on various NLP tasks.

Subword tokenization methods like Byte-Pair Encoding enable handling of rare and unseen words. We show that subword units provide a good balance between character and word-level representations for language modeling.

We introduce positional encodings that inject information about token positions into transformer models. Using sinusoidal functions or learned embeddings, positional encodings enable transformers to capture sequence order.

Layer normalization normalizes inputs across features rather than batch examples. We show that layer normalization stabilizes training of recurrent and transformer networks, enabling faster convergence.
We present neural image captioning models that generate natural language descriptions of images. Using CNN encoders and RNN decoders with attention, these models produce human-quality captions.

Visual question answering combines computer vision and natural language processing to answer questions about images. We introduce models that jointly reason over visual and linguistic information to generate accurate answers.

We present neural text-to-speech models that generate natural-sounding speech from text. Using sequence-to-sequence architectures with attention, these models achieve human-like prosody and pronunciation.

Speech recognition models based on deep learning convert audio to text. We introduce end-to-end models that learn directly from spectrograms, eliminating the need for hand-crafted features and achieving state-of-the-art accuracy.

We present neural collaborative filtering for recommender systems. By learning user and item embeddings with neural networks, these models capture complex user-item interactions and improve recommendation quality.

Anomaly detection identifies unusual patterns in data. We introduce autoencoder-based methods that learn compressed representations of normal data, enabling detection of anomalies through reconstruction error.
Time series forecasting predicts future values based on historical data. We present neural models including LSTMs and transformers that capture temporal dependencies and achieve accurate predictions.

We introduce neural methods for program synthesis that generate code from specifications. By training on large corpora of code, these models learn programming patterns and can generate functional programs.

Neural theorem proving aims to automatically prove mathematical theorems. We present models that learn to search proof spaces and select tactics, making progress toward automated mathematical reasoning.
We present neural models for knowledge graph completion that predict missing links between entities. Using embeddings and relation modeling, these methods improve knowledge base quality and coverage.

Multi-hop reasoning requires combining information from multiple sources to answer questions. We introduce models with iterative attention mechanisms that perform multiple reasoning steps over knowledge bases or documents.
We present neural fact-checking models that verify claims against evidence. Using natural language inference and retrieval, these models detect misinformation and assess claim veracity.

Dialogue systems engage in natural language conversations with users. We introduce neural models that maintain context, generate coherent responses, and complete goal-oriented tasks through conversation.

We present neural code completion models that predict code tokens as developers type. Trained on large code repositories, these models understand programming language syntax and common coding patterns.
Bug detection aims to identify software defects automatically. We introduce neural models trained on code and bug reports that learn to recognize bug patterns and predict potential issues.
We present neural models for code summarization that generate natural language descriptions of code. These models help developers understand unfamiliar code by producing human-readable summaries.
Program repair aims to automatically fix software bugs. We introduce neural models that learn to generate patches by training on past bug fixes, achieving promising results on benchmark datasets.

We present neural machine translation models with improved handling of rare words. Using copy mechanisms and subword units, these models maintain translation quality even for low-resource language pairs.

Document-level translation considers context beyond individual sentences. We introduce models with document-level encoders that capture discourse structure, improving translation coherence and accuracy.

We present multilingual neural machine translation models that translate between multiple language pairs using a single model. Parameter sharing across languages enables zero-shot translation and improves low-resource translation.

Unsupervised machine translation learns to translate without parallel data. We introduce methods using monolingual data and cross-lingual embeddings that achieve reasonable translation quality without aligned texts.
We present neural models for automatic post-editing that improve machine translation output. By learning from human corrections, these models fix systematic errors and enhance translation quality.

Neural language generation aims to produce coherent, fluent text. We introduce planning-based approaches that first generate content plans and then realize them as natural language, improving output quality.

We present controllable text generation methods that allow specifying desired attributes like sentiment, topic, or style. Using conditional language models and attribute classifiers, these methods enable fine-grained generation control.
Commonsense reasoning requires background knowledge about the world. We introduce models that incorporate commonsense knowledge bases and demonstrate improved performance on reasoning benchmarks.

We present neural models for mathematical reasoning that solve word problems and prove theorems. By combining language understanding with symbolic reasoning, these models make progress on mathematical tasks.

Scientific document understanding aims to extract information from research papers. We introduce models for citation analysis, claim extraction, and method identification that assist scientific literature review.
We present neural models for biomedical text mining that extract entities, relations, and events from medical literature. These models accelerate drug discovery and medical knowledge extraction.

Legal document analysis uses NLP to process contracts, case law, and regulations. We introduce models for legal entity recognition, argument mining, and document classification that assist legal professionals.
We present neural models for financial text analysis including sentiment analysis of news and earnings calls. These models help predict market movements and assess financial risk.

Social media analysis extracts insights from platforms like Twitter and Facebook. We introduce models for stance detection, hate speech identification, and trend analysis that understand social discourse.

We present multimodal models that process images, text, audio, and video jointly. By learning shared representations across modalities, these models enable applications like video captioning and audio-visual speech recognition.

Neural architecture adaptation automatically adjusts model capacity to computational constraints. We introduce methods that find optimal architectures for target devices, balancing accuracy and efficiency.

We present neural compression techniques that reduce model size through pruning, quantization, and knowledge distillation. These methods enable deployment of large models on resource-constrained devices.

Lifelong learning enables models to continuously learn from new data without forgetting previous knowledge. We introduce methods that selectively retain important parameters while adapting to new tasks.

We present fairness-aware machine learning methods that mitigate bias in model predictions. By incorporating fairness constraints during training, these methods reduce discrimination and improve equity.

Privacy-preserving machine learning protects sensitive data during model training and inference. We introduce differential privacy and federated learning techniques that enable learning while preserving privacy.

We present interpretable machine learning methods that provide human-understandable explanations for model predictions. Using attention visualization and feature attribution, these methods increase model transparency.

Neural architecture efficiency focuses on reducing computational cost and memory usage. We introduce methods for model compression, efficient operators, and hardware-aware design that enable faster inference.

We present self-supervised learning methods for speech that learn representations from unlabeled audio. By pre-training on large unlabeled datasets, these models achieve strong performance on downstream speech tasks.

Cross-modal retrieval aims to search for items in one modality using queries in another. We introduce models that learn joint embeddings enabling image-text retrieval and other cross-modal matching tasks.

We present neural methods for music generation that create melodies, harmonies, and complete compositions. Using sequence models and hierarchical representations, these systems produce musically coherent outputs.

Video understanding aims to extract semantic information from videos. We introduce models for action recognition, video captioning, and temporal localization that process spatiotemporal information effectively.

We present neural models for 3D computer vision including object detection, semantic segmentation, and scene understanding in three dimensions. These models process point clouds and voxel grids for 3D reasoning.
Optical character recognition converts images of text to machine-readable text. We introduce end-to-end neural OCR models that handle complex layouts and achieve high accuracy on diverse documents.
We present neural models for sketch recognition and generation. By learning from large sketch datasets, these models understand abstract visual representations and enable sketch-based interfaces.

Neural style transfer for video maintains temporal consistency while applying artistic styles. We introduce methods that process video sequences coherently, avoiding flickering and temporal artifacts.
We present neural models for depth estimation from single images. Using convolutional networks trained on RGB-D data, these models predict per-pixel depth and enable 3D scene understanding.
Pose estimation determines the position and orientation of objects or people. We introduce neural models that detect keypoints and estimate 3D poses from images and videos.

We present neural models for human activity recognition from sensor data. Using accelerometers and gyroscopes, these models classify activities and enable health monitoring and context-aware applications.
Neural recommendation systems personalize content by learning user preferences. We introduce deep learning approaches that model complex user-item interactions and improve recommendation quality.
We present neural models for fraud detection in financial transactions. By learning patterns of fraudulent behavior, these models identify suspicious activities and prevent financial losses.
Medical image analysis uses deep learning for diagnosis and treatment planning. We introduce models for disease detection, organ segmentation, and lesion characterization that assist radiologists.
We present neural models for drug discovery that predict molecular properties and generate novel compounds. These models accelerate pharmaceutical research and reduce development costs.
Neural weather forecasting predicts atmospheric conditions using deep learning. We introduce models that process satellite imagery and sensor data, improving prediction accuracy and lead time.
We present neural models for traffic prediction that forecast congestion and travel times. Using spatiotemporal data from sensors and GPS, these models enable intelligent transportation systems.

Energy forecasting predicts electricity demand and renewable energy generation. We introduce neural models that consider weather, historical patterns, and external factors to optimize grid operations.
We present neural models for earthquake prediction that analyze seismic data. While long-term prediction remains challenging, these models improve early warning systems and hazard assessment.

Agricultural AI uses computer vision and sensor data to optimize farming. We introduce models for crop disease detection, yield prediction, and automated harvesting that improve agricultural productivity.

We present neural models for climate modeling that predict long-term climate patterns. By learning from historical data and physical simulations, these models inform climate policy and adaptation strategies.
